units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: MegaETH and HyperEVM: indirect evidence for three PoolManager code paths their producers have never run
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 39 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1371, L-1372 and L-1374. Cycle 39 established, per site, what a wrong result would do in PoolManager code that the block producers of MegaETH and HyperEVM have never executed inside the PoolManager. Four sites can only revert or cost the caller. Three would be paid from the shared balance and can be reached by any account today: site B, the wide branch of getAmount1Delta (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252; pcs 22585, 22639, 23094 of the runtime), in a hookless pool the account creates from native currency and a currency other pools hold, for about 2.9e10 wei; donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480; pcs 10223 to 10513), in any existing pool for 1 unit; and exact-output swaps (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:88-104 with SqrtPriceMath.sol:158-177) on HyperEVM in existing pools. RPC nodes, replicas and the reference interpreter return the right words for all three. Nothing suggests a fault. What is missing is evidence about the code that produces blocks, and only a mined transaction gives that directly; this review sends none. This theme looks for the next best evidence in what is already mined. The critic's observation: every MULMOD of the PoolManager that takes one operand from a PUSH literal in its own basic block is in the never-run set (modulus 2^128 at pc 22378, modulus 10^6 at pc 22513, modulus 2^96 at pc 22639 which is site B, multiplicand 2^96 at pcs 20958, 22721 and 22763), while the three MULMOD sites the producers did run with a wide product take every operand from the stack. A producer that compiles code and specialises constant operands (as revmc's constant folding and peephole passes do, and as the public MegaETH compiler source does for some opcodes, F-166) lowers exactly these sites differently, so wide MULMOD runs with stack operands elsewhere say nothing about them. Scripts and data: research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-closed-producer-operand-census.work (scripts census_tracer.js, classes.py, pmsites.py, pminv.py, aggregate.py; the per-block census of 40,940 validated MegaETH blocks is in runs/*/census.txt.gz if still on disk, 2.2 GB, read it as a stream and do not copy it), research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-hyperevm-producer-census.work/scripts (shape_tracer.js, census.py, agg.py, inv.py), research/network-risk/cycles/039/theme-never-run-sites-shared-balance.work/scripts (reach39.py, logs39.py, build39.py), the MegaETH stateless validator build of research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work, opcodes/jumpmap.json and research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json. Disk space is short: keep counts and examples, not traces. Task 1 (L-1371): from the PoolManager runtime list every MULMOD, MUL, DIV, MOD, SHL, SHR, AND and EXP whose operand comes from a PUSH literal in the same basic block, with pc, literal and src/ line, and mark which are in the never-run set of each producer. Then count, in the MegaETH validated-block census and in the HyperEVM replica traces, executions in any contract of a MULMOD with a product of 2^256 or more where the modulus or a multiplicand was pushed as a literal in the same block, split by literal (2^96, 2^128, 10^6, 2^256-1, other) and position. If the stored census did not record where operands came from, extend the tracer to look back to the producing opcode and rerun it over as many blocks as time allows, newest first, and over every block with a Uniswap v3 or v4 style swap. A count of zero for a literal means no evidence exists that the producer lowers that constant correctly; say so per literal. Task 2 (L-1372): find contracts on MegaETH and on HyperEVM whose code contains the same byte sequences as the PoolManager's basic blocks for site B (pcs 22544 to 22660), donate (pcs 10223 to 10518) and the exact-output step (pcs 20618 to 20840): another deployment of the 24,009 byte runtime, a v4 fork built with the same compiler settings, or a contract that inlines the same library code (FullMath.mulDiv compiled by solc 0.8.26 via IR gives recognisable blocks; Uniswap v3 pools compiled by 0.7.6 do not match byte for byte but exercise the same arithmetic). Search the code of every address seen in the traces for the 64-byte windows around pcs 22639, 10491 and 20672. For each match say whether a mined transaction executed that block, with what operands, and whether the result was accepted by the validator or replicas. Task 3 (L-1374): run the public stateless validator, or failing that debug_traceBlockByNumber with the pc-level tracer, over every MegaETH block with a PoolManager log from 32,987,130 to head, and over the HyperEVM blocks with a PoolManager log since cycle 37, and report per pc of the never-run set (22378, 22513, 22639, 22721, 22763, 10491, 10513, 23924 and the exact-output pcs on HyperEVM) whether it has now executed and with which operands. One mined run with the reference result closes that site for that producer. Task 4: for each of the three sites and each producer, state what evidence now exists, in order of strength: a mined run inside the PoolManager; a mined run of byte-identical code elsewhere; mined runs of the same opcode with the same literal operand; mined runs of the same opcode with stack operands only; none. Then write the short instruction a deployer could follow to close what remains with its own transactions before launch (which call, which pool, which amounts, what to read afterwards and the value it must equal); do not send anything yourself. Task 5: nothing here is a finding unless a mined result differs from the reference; if one does, give the block, the transaction, the words and who lost what. Otherwise record counts and matches as cleared and keep one lead per site and producer that still has no mined run. Say for the other 19 networks that this theme does not apply.

Task 5: plant at least five faults in the block runs (a high limb dropped in the wide product, the literal 2^96 modulus replaced by 2^95, a rounding branch inverted, the fee growth quotient truncated to 128 bits, a stale stack slot at block entry) and show each is caught on these inputs. This theme concerns Monad only; say so for the other 20 networks.
